A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same shortest-path reasoning study. Their text, equations, Figures 1–10, Table 1, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison despite reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformer-training experiments, shortest-path accuracy, reasoning-trace diagnostics, temperature sweeps, and model-size/data-scale ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports additional exploration-order surprisal measurements and longer-training evaluations.

M1.justification: The trace-generation algorithm, custom tokenization, Phi3 architecture, and masked next-token objective are retained. Section 3 clarifies queue handling and randomized repetition, without establishing a different underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic layered-DAG shortest-path task with the same graph-generation parameters and graph-depth coverage. No new dataset, domain, or test population is introduced.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain direct question-answer training, efficient DP traces, inefficient DFS traces, intermediate η = 0 traces, and deterministic/randomized redundancy variants. The appendix model-size and data-scale comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the reported reasoning-trace context length from 2048 to 4096 tokens. Figure 6 extends evaluation to 40 epochs and replaces the nine-temperature table with four temperatures at epochs 20 and 40; Section 4 also adds a surprisal measure. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analysis of exploration-choice unpredictability using average surprisal and extends the investigation of whether excessive trace length persists with longer training. It removes v1's numerical breakdown of the early 'eureka' transition, while retaining the appendix trace-quality and scaling analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 4(c)'s caption changes from three to five seed-specific training-loss trajectories. Both versions already specify five-seed, one-sigma reporting generally, so this does not establish an across-the-board increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: Results are updated within the retained experiments: Figure 5(b)'s RR accuracy changes from 18% to 8% at T = 0 and from 81% to 84% at T = 1. V2 also adds surprisal estimates and 40-epoch results, revises several curves, and removes transition-specific percentages. The principal trace-ranking conclusions persist; the changed context setting prevents treating these updates as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The graph formulation, trace constraints, and computational-complexity reasoning are retained. The new surprisal measurements apply a standard information measure without adding a theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same central claims: intermediate reasoning helps, inefficient structured traces can outperform efficient ones, length alone is insufficient, and next-token confidence correlates with learnability.

C2.justification: Section 4 shifts emphasis from intuitive continuity or 'inertia' toward measured differences in exploration-choice uncertainty. It also qualifies excessive verbosity as an initial tendency that can diminish with longer training, rather than simply describing convergence toward inefficient trace lengths. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access URL in the abstract, makes queue handling more explicit, and revises the context-window specification in Appendix A.1. The optimizer, hardware, precision, data-generation instructions, and train/test split disclosures otherwise remain stable.

R1.justification: V2 drops v1's specific connection between favorable sampling temperatures and DeepSeek-R1's recommended temperature range. This is a limited removal of a comparison with prior work; the same 49 cited works and the broader positioning in Section 5 are retained.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization is retained. Local revisions clarify the generator and results narrative, consistently add DP/DFS labels, and update the front matter and author order.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from the wider preprint format to a narrower NeurIPS layout, with redistributed figures and substantially reflowed tables. Figure 1's graph is redrawn, Figures 3–4 gain legends, and Figure 6 receives extended axes and an epoch-grouped table. This is a substantial presentation revision despite retaining the same numbered figures and table.

improvement.justification: The added surprisal analysis and 40-epoch results better support the predictability explanation and qualify the persistence of verbosity bias. Clearer legends and a code-access link also help readers. These gains outweigh the limited loss of transition-specific diagnostics, although the context-window revision remains unexplained and the central contribution and coverage are unchanged.
